lessons.title: Angles on a line
lessons.label: Angles on a line
lessons.objective: Use a straight angle to find a missing adjacent angle.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Calling adjacent angles on a straight line complementary; they sum to 180, not 90.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why must the two angles add to one hundred and eighty degrees?

steps.title: A straight angle is half a turn
steps.explanation: Angles meeting on this straight line fill a half turn.

scene.description: A half-turn sector measuring one hundred and eighty degrees.

steps.title: Show the known angle

left.text: {{angle|words}} degrees plus unknown equals one hundred and eighty degrees
left.spoken: {{angle|words}} degrees plus unknown equals one hundred and eighty degrees

steps.explanation: The blue angle is {{angle|words}} degrees. The purple angle fills the rest.

scene.description: Adjacent sectors of {{angle|words}} degrees and an unknown angle fill the straight angle.

steps.title: Find the rest of the half turn

left.text: one hundred and eighty minus {{angle|words}} equals {{missing|words}} degrees
left.spoken: one hundred and eighty minus {{angle|words}} equals {{missing|words}} degrees

steps.explanation: Subtract the known angle from the straight angle. The missing angle is {{missing|words}} degrees.

scene.description: The two adjacent angles measure {{angle|words}} and {{missing|words}} degrees.

lessons.title: Rectangle area
lessons.label: Rectangle area
lessons.objective: Connect rows of unit squares to length times width.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Using boundary units instead of square units for area.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why is this answer in square units rather than units?

steps.title: Area measures the inside
steps.explanation: Cover the rectangle with equal unit squares, without gaps or overlaps.

scene.description: A rectangle {{width}} units wide and {{height}} units high.

$if.then: Each row contains {{width|words}} unit squares. One row covers {{width|words}} square units.
$if.else: Each row contains {{width|words}} unit squares. {{n}} rows cover {{filled}} square units.

scene.description: {{n}} complete rows of {{width|words}} shaded unit squares.

steps.title: {{height|Words}} rows of {{width|words}} make {{area|words}}
steps.explanation: The area is {{area|words}} square units. Each small square is one square unit.

scene.description: A rectangle {{width}} units wide and {{height}} units high.

lessons.title: Angles around a point
lessons.label: Angles around a point
lessons.objective: Use a full turn to find the remaining angle around a point.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Using 180 for a full turn around a point.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: How is a full turn different from a straight angle?

steps.title: Start with the first angle
steps.explanation: The first angle covers part of a full turn.

scene.description: A {{angle|words}} degree sector.

steps.title: Add the next angle
steps.explanation: A right angle adds ninety degrees. Together the known angles cover {{known|words}} degrees.

scene.description: The two known sectors total {{known|words}} degrees.

steps.title: Complete the full turn

left.text: three hundred and sixty minus {{known|words}} equals {{missing|words}} degrees
left.spoken: three hundred and sixty minus {{known|words}} equals {{missing|words}} degrees

steps.explanation: The remaining angle is {{missing|words}} degrees. The three angles make a full turn.

scene.description: Angles of {{angle|words}}, ninety and {{missing|words}} degrees make three hundred and sixty degrees.

lessons.title: Rectangle perimeter
lessons.label: Rectangle perimeter
lessons.objective: Find perimeter by adding all {{height|words}} boundary lengths.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Multiplying length by width gives perimeter.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why must both long sides and both short sides be counted?

steps.title: Perimeter measures the boundary
steps.explanation: Walk around the outside. Count each of the four sides once.

scene.description: A rectangle {{width}} units wide and {{height}} units high.

steps.title: Count the top side
steps.explanation: The top side is {{width|words}} units long.

scene.description: A rectangle {{width}} units wide and {{height}} units high.

steps.title: Count the right side
steps.explanation: The right side is {{height|words}} units long.

scene.description: A rectangle {{width}} units wide and {{height}} units high.

steps.title: Count the bottom side
steps.explanation: The bottom side is {{width|words}} units long.

scene.description: A rectangle {{width}} units wide and {{height}} units high.

steps.title: Count the left side
steps.explanation: The left side is {{height|words}} units long.

scene.description: A rectangle {{width}} units wide and {{height}} units high.

steps.title: Add all four side lengths
steps.explanation: The perimeter is {{perimeter|words}} units. This measures length around the edge, not the space inside.

scene.description: A rectangle {{width}} units wide and {{height}} units high.

lessons.title: Triangle area
lessons.label: Triangle area
lessons.objective: Explain the factor one half by completing a rectangle with a congruent triangle.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Using the sloping side instead of the perpendicular height.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why does adding a congruent triangle help us find the area?

steps.title: Start with a right triangle
steps.explanation: The base and perpendicular height are {{base|words}} and {{height|words}} units.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular base {{base|words}} and height {{height|words}}.

steps.title: Add one congruent triangle
steps.explanation: A second triangle of exactly the same shape and size completes the rectangle.

scene.description: Two congruent right triangles fill a {{base|words}} by {{height|words}} rectangle.

steps.title: Take half the rectangle
steps.explanation: The rectangle has {{rectangle|words}} square units. Each congruent triangle has half: {{area|words}}.

scene.description: Two congruent right triangles fill a {{base|words}} by {{height|words}} rectangle.

lessons.title: Pythagoras: square areas
lessons.label: Pythagoras: square areas
lessons.objective: Connect the two smaller square areas to the hypotenuse square in a {{a|words}}-{{b|words}}-{{c|words}} example.
prerequisites: Square numbers and square roots; recognise a right angle.

tutorNotes.observe: Let the student describe the visible change before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Adding the side lengths directly rather than adding their squares.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why do we compare {{aa|words}} plus {{bb|words}} with {{cc|words}} rather than {{a|words}} plus {{b|words}} with {{c|words}}?

steps.title: Find the right angle and hypotenuse
steps.explanation: The perpendicular sides are {{a|words}} and {{b|words}}. The opposite, longest side is {{c|words}}: the hypotenuse c.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides {{a}} and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Build the first square
steps.explanation: The square on the {{a|words}}-unit side has {{aa|words}} unit tiles.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides {{a}} and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}. Known square areas: a: {{aa}}.
scene.caption: Unit tiles show areas; outlines keep their original sizes.

steps.title: Build the second square
steps.explanation: The square on the {{b|words}}-unit side has {{bb|words}} unit tiles.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides {{a}} and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}. Known square areas: a: {{aa}}, b: {{bb}}.
scene.caption: Unit tiles show areas; outlines keep their original sizes.

steps.title: Build the hypotenuse square
steps.explanation: The square on the {{c|words}}-unit hypotenuse has room for {{cc|words}} unit tiles.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides {{a}} and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}. Known square areas: a: {{aa}}, b: {{bb}}, c: {{cc}}.
scene.caption: Unit tiles show areas; outlines keep their original sizes.

steps.title: Compare the same total area
steps.explanation: Move the {{aa|words}} and {{bb|words}} unit tiles into the largest square. They fit without gaps or overlaps; no tile changes size.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides {{a}} and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}. Known square areas: a: {{aa}}, b: {{bb}}, c: {{cc}}.
scene.caption: Unit tiles show areas; outlines keep their original sizes.

steps.title: State the square-area relationship
steps.explanation: Pythagoras relates square areas on a right triangle. This example illustrates the theorem; checking one example is not a general proof.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides {{a}} and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}. Known square areas: a: {{aa}}, b: {{bb}}, c: {{cc}}.
scene.caption: Unit tiles show areas; outlines keep their original sizes.

constraints.message: Keep the unit-tile transfer within a five-unit square.

lessons.title: Find the hypotenuse
lessons.label: Find the hypotenuse
lessons.objective: Square perpendicular sides, add square areas, then take a positive root.
prerequisites: Understand square areas on a right triangle and principal square roots.

tutorNotes.observe: Let the student describe the visible change before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Stopping at {{cc|words}}, or taking the square root before adding areas.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why is {{cc|words}} an area, while {{c|words}} is a length?

steps.title: Identify the unknown longest side

left.text: a equals {{a|words}}, b equals {{b|words}}, c unknown
left.spoken: a equals {{a|words}}, b equals {{b|words}}, c unknown

steps.explanation: The unknown c is opposite the marked right angle. It is the hypotenuse.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides {{a}} and {{b}}, and hypotenuse unknown c.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Use the square-area relationship

left.text: {{a|words}} squared plus {{b|words}} squared equals c squared
left.spoken: {{a|words}} squared plus {{b|words}} squared equals c squared

steps.explanation: For a right triangle, the two smaller square areas add to the hypotenuse square area.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides {{a}} and {{b}}, and hypotenuse unknown c.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Square the first shorter side
steps.explanation: {{a|Words}} squared is {{aa|words}}.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides {{a}} and {{b}}, and hypotenuse unknown c. Known square areas: a: {{aa}}.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Square the other shorter side
steps.explanation: {{b|Words}} squared is {{bb|words}}.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides {{a}} and {{b}}, and hypotenuse unknown c. Known square areas: a: {{aa}}, b: {{bb}}.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Add the two square areas
steps.explanation: {{aa|Words}} plus {{bb|words}} is {{cc|words}}. This is an area, not the side length.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides {{a}} and {{b}}, and hypotenuse unknown c. Known square areas: a: {{aa}}, b: {{bb}}, c: {{cc}}.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Take the positive square root

left.text: c equals the square root of {{cc|words}}, which is {{c|words}}
left.spoken: c equals the square root of {{cc|words}}, which is {{c|words}}

steps.explanation: The side length is the positive square root of its square area. The hypotenuse is {{c|words}} units, longer than {{a|words}} or {{b|words}}.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides {{a}} and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}. Known square areas: a: {{aa}}, b: {{bb}}, c: {{cc}}.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

lessons.title: Find a shorter side
lessons.label: Find a shorter side
lessons.objective: Subtract a known square area from the hypotenuse square before taking a positive root.
prerequisites: Square roots; subtract the same amount from both sides of an equation.

tutorNotes.observe: Let the student describe the visible change before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Adding {{b|words}} squared and {{c|words}} squared when the hypotenuse is already known.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why does this example need subtraction rather than addition?

steps.title: The hypotenuse is already known

left.text: b equals {{b|words}}, c equals {{c|words}}, a unknown
left.spoken: b equals {{b|words}}, c equals {{c|words}}, a unknown

steps.explanation: {{c|Words}} is the hypotenuse, opposite the right angle. The unknown a is a shorter side.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides unknown a and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Set up the square areas

left.text: a squared plus {{b|words}} squared equals {{c|words}} squared
left.spoken: a squared plus {{b|words}} squared equals {{c|words}} squared

steps.explanation: The two smaller squares together have the same area as the hypotenuse square.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides unknown a and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Square the hypotenuse
steps.explanation: {{c|Words}} squared is {{cc|words}}.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides unknown a and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}. Known square areas: c: {{cc}}.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Square the known shorter side
steps.explanation: {{b|Words}} squared is {{bb|words}}.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides unknown a and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}. Known square areas: b: {{bb}}, c: {{cc}}.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Find the remaining square area
steps.explanation: Subtract {{bb|words}} from both sides. The unknown square is the remaining part of the hypotenuse square area.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides unknown a and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}. Known square areas: b: {{bb}}, c: {{cc}}.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Calculate the difference
steps.explanation: {{cc|Words}} minus {{bb|words}} leaves {{aa|words}} square units.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides unknown a and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}. Known square areas: a: {{aa}}, b: {{bb}}, c: {{cc}}.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

steps.title: Take the positive square root

left.text: a equals square root of {{aa|words}}, which is {{a|words}}
left.spoken: a equals square root of {{aa|words}}, which is {{a|words}}

steps.explanation: The shorter side is {{a|words}} units. We subtracted because one square area was missing from a known total.

scene.description: A right triangle with perpendicular sides {{a}} and {{b}}, and hypotenuse {{c}}. Known square areas: a: {{aa}}, b: {{bb}}, c: {{cc}}.
scene.caption: The small corner marker is a right angle: 90 degrees.

constraints.message: Keep the shorter side within the supported drawing bounds.
